claims.text: For rectangular data \((r,q,i,j)=(2,6,1,1)\), the LR presentation has \(27\) basis elements and \(327\) relation vectors; its computed SNF has \(25\) unit factors and no nonunit factors, so \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^2\). [artifact bfbfd736e27f1a193b24aab07cfae4f512c6c9dd5039963e396331b46516f16f]

For rectangular data \((r,q,i,j)=(5,2,1,1)\), the LR presentation has \(20\) basis elements and \(179\) relation vectors; its computed SNF has \(18\) unit factors and no nonunit factors, so \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^2\). [artifact bfbfd736e27f1a193b24aab07cfae4f512c6c9dd5039963e396331b46516f16f]

In both cases \(a=b=1\), hence \(N=2\), and the two candidate families specialize to \(\{s_{(1)},s_{(2)}\}\) and \(\{s_{(1)},s_{(1,1)}\}\). Conditional on the established generation theorem and the two computed cokernels, each family is irredundant: deletion would make \(\mathbb Z^2\) cyclic, which is impossible.
These computations concern rectangular Schur-data only; no permutation \(v_{r,s,t,n}\) admissibility is asserted.
